label: text
text: COAL DEVELOPMENTS RAPIDLY IMPROVE.

label: paragraph_title
text: MINERS TO DECIDE

label: text
text: Negotiations for the settlement of the coal dispute have been taking place to-day at Downing Street, and there have been rapid developments.

label: text
text: The Mediation Committee of the Trade Union Congress was received this morning by Mr. S. Baldwin, Prime Minister and the full Cabinet Coal Committee. The mediators stated that the Miners' Executive had authorised them to accept district agreements as a basis of negotiation, providing that there were safeguards that the same national principles, which were embodied in the last national agreements should run through all district agreements.

label: text
text:
The Prime Minister, after leaving the Mediation Committee, consented to receive the Miners' Executive. Accordingly the "miners' leaders arrived at Downing Street and the Mediation Committee left, one of them saying: "Negotiations have definitely been opened and we are now leaving it to the miners."
The discussion between the members of the Government and the miners' leaders was adjourned for lunch and was resumed later in the day.

label: text
text: Meanwhile, it is understood that the Government has been in touch with the Coal Owners' Association. When the miner's leaders left Downing Street this evening it was announced that the discussion would be resumed tomorrow afternoon.

label: text
text: It is expected that the coal owners will visit Downing Street between now and then.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text:
London, November 5.
Peace prospects are brightening,
following an interview of the
Trade Union Congress delegation
with the Cabinet Coal Committee at
10. Downing Street, at noon. The
miners' executive called at Downing Street at one o'clock to see the
Premier. — Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Facing the Facts.
Rugby, Nov. 5.

label: text
text: Members of the Trade Union Congress Committee who are mediating in the coal dispute proceeded to Downing Street at noon to-day for a conference with the Premier and other members of the Government. This step was taken after a meeting between the Committee and the Miners' Executive. The position seems to be that the executive, having faced the facts of the situation are now prepared to agree to the negotiation of district agreements without restriction other than that such agreements should be governed by arrangements capable of national application.

label: text
text:
The purpose of the meeting between the Trade Union mediators and the Government now proceeding is presumably to ascertain definitely to what extent the Government are prepared to support a settlement on these lines. If assurance satisfactory to the miners are obtained, a resolution in favour of resuming negotiation for an immediate settlement will be put before the Miners' Delegates Conference later to-day.
At present the position is thus much more hopeful and speedy developments are anticipated although the road is not yet troop from serious obstacles and the attitude of collery owners is the moment rather obscure.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text:
Coul peace negotiations have been definitely opened, stated Mr. Citrine Secretary of the Trades Union Congress, on leaving Downing Street, where the Miners' Executive are conferring with the Prime Minister. "We are now leaving it to the miners, having opened the door to a settlement."—Reuter.
Hopeful Position.
London, Nov. 5.
The Cabinet and the miners resume negotiations to-morrow.
One of the Trades Union Congress mediators says that the position is more hopeful than since the stoppage began.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: BOLOGNA SEQUEL.

label: text
text:
DRASTIC MEASURES ENFORCED
IN ITALY.

label: text
text: ANTI-FASCIST CAMPAIGN

label: text
text: Indignation throughout Italy in consequence of the attempt to assassinate Signor Mussolini in Bologna is the subject of a report by the Minister of the Interior to the Cabinet which approved of his drastic measures for public safety us follows:

label: text
text: The revision of all passports for abroad and the cancellation from November 9 of all passports issued except those possessed by Italians abroad.

label: text
text: Severe "penalties, including the use of armed, force, for anyone attempting to leave or abetting attempts to leave Italy without a passport."

label: text
text: The suppression sine die of all publications opposed to the present regime.

label: text
text: The dissolution of all parties, societies, and organisations having anti-Fascist aims.

label: text
text: The strictest Police supervision of those who have committed or who have shown an intention of committing acts likely violently to subvert the social and economic institutions of the country and endanger the safety of the State.

label: text
text: Severe penalties for anyone illegally wearing a uniform or insignia of any institutions especially Fuscist organisations.

label: text
text:
The creation of a Political Inves-
ignation Department attached to
each Faseist Command.

label: paragraph_title
text: Attempts On High Persons.

label: text
text:
The Minister of Justice explained and the Cabinet approved of a Bill for the defence of the State establishing the death penalty for anyone committing an act against the life, health, or personal liberty of the King, Regent, Queen, Crown Prince, or chief of the Government, also any act calculated to lead to the subjection of the State to a foreign Power, affect the independence of the State, or compromise its unity, and anyone revealing or procuring political or military secrets or committing acts calculated to cause armed risings or participating therein, or on anyone inciting civil war or pillage.
Complicity in some of the above-mentioned crimes is punishable by 15 to 30 years' solitary confinement. The instigating of such crimes by means of the Press or their condonation is punishable by solitary confinement of five to 15 years.

label: paragraph_title
text: Dangerous Societies

label: text
text:
The reconstitution under new names of Societies that have been dissolved renders the authors liable to solitary confinement for three to 10 years. Members or propagandists on behalf of such Societies are similarly liable to two to five years. Any national outside Italian territory spreading false news regarding the internal conditions of the State is liable to solitary confinement for five to 15 years.
Sentences in default render the offenders liable to the loss of the right of citizenship and the confiscation of their property.
The foregoing crimes will be tried by special tribunals of regu

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: EMPIRE ECONOMICS.

label: text
text: INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIATION REPORT.

label: text
text: ADVANTAGE TO COMMERCE.

label: text
text:
Several reports submitted by the Economic Committee of the Imperial Conference were approved by the meeting of the conference at a brief session this morning.
Those include a report on industrial standardisation within the Empire which states that the Committee was much impressed with the advantages that would accrue also to manufacturers and to buyers of goods to which the principle of standardisation was applied. It is recognised, however, not only that the principle of standardisation can be less advantageously applied in some industries than in others, but also that it is not one to be applied indiscriminately.

label: text
text: In particular the report points out that it is important to beware of the risk of impeding technical progress, and to see that suitable provisions for adequate revision are not overlooked.

label: text
text: A considerable amount of progress has been made within the Empire both in the extension of standardisation and in securing common standards, but the belief is expressed that much more could be done to the advantage of trade within the Empire and to the trade with the world at large. It is, therefore, recommended to the favourable consideration of the several Governments of the Empire that they should take steps to promote the further development of standardisation; should arrange for the exchange of information with other parts of the Empire; and, when common standards are possible and mutually advantageous, should co-operate, with other parts of the Empire in regard thereto.

label: paragraph_title
text: Wool Statistic

label: text
text: The report on wpol statistics approved by the Conference contained the following resolution:—

label: text
text: “The Imperial Conference, impressed by the need for more complete, more uniform, and more prompt statistics regarding production, stocks, and consumption of wool throughout the world commends that such steps as are found to be most suitable should be taken to secure the co-operation of foreign countries in this matter; and, further, that the Governments of the Empire should consider the adoption of such measures as are necessary and feasible to secure the provision and publication of such statistics, provided that the foreign countries materially concerned either as producers or consumers are prepared to take similar action.”

label: paragraph_title
text: Foodstuffs.

label: text
text: A further report approved by the Conference contained a resolution in the following terms:—

label: text
text: The conference, impressed by the need for international statistics of quantities of foodstuffs held in cold storage, recommends that suitable steps should be taken to obtain the co-operation of foreign countries in securing the compilation and prompt publication of such international statistics." — British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: PROFANE LANGUAGE ON THE BENCH.

label: text
text: Washington, November 5.

label: text
text: Judge George English of Eastern Illinois, has resigned owing to proceedings against him on charges of manipulation of bankruptcy funds, and the usurpation of his power to use profane language on the bench. President Coolidge has accepted his resignation. The case, therefore, is now regarded as closed.—Reuter's American Service.
